stage: simulation plan, step 2 (frozen before any simulation code or run)
purpose: Check, without LLM calls, whether any admission rule meets the Go criteria at a Dev-B budget the project can run. This tests the statistical validity of the existing rules; it is not meant to show that C6 is better. A No-Go is a result.
decisions: David, 2026-11-24 (scope) and 2026-11-25 (cell bounds, values, borderline rule)

notation.p10: share of pairs where the candidate succeeds and S0 fails (improvement)
notation.p01: share of pairs where the candidate fails and S0 succeeds (regression)
notation.delta: p10 - p01, per cell (delta_c) and as the equal-weight mean over cells (delta)

metric: CD (correct_disposition) only. ES is not simulated: S0's ES is at the floor or the ceiling in every 009b cell (audit_013).

inputs_allowed.rule: Only S0 records, the Ticket 012 stage-0 records of S0-prime and the v1 public results. 009b Dev-B and Oracle candidate outcomes are not read.
inputs_allowed.s0_extreme_rates: runs/calibration + runs/t009_calibration, S0 bf65e569ae37, 420 cases x repeats 0-4; case-level rate = mean over the five repeats
inputs_allowed.s0_prime_rates: runs/t012_stage0, _rerun1, _rerun2, S0-prime 3665eab231d6, Dev-A 60 cases; case-level rate = mean over the three runs
inputs_allowed.empirical_effects: results/ticket-005/analysis.json, the 12 proposer candidates, oracle CD cell effects (as in evidencegate.t009.power_sim)
inputs_allowed.existing_code: src/evidencegate/t009/power_sim.py is extended, not replaced. Before any new condition runs, the extension must reproduce the null label rates of the 009b pre-registration section 9.1 (Local Harm 0.167, Severe 0.000475); if it does not, stop.

simulated_data.baseline_cases: per cell, n_c case-level rates drawn with replacement from the cell's case-level rates of the chosen baseline
simulated_data.candidate_rates: case rate + the candidate's delta_c for that cell, clipped to [0, 1]
simulated_data.dev_b: S0 and each candidate run once per case (Bernoulli of the case rate); S0's run is the one every candidate is paired with
simulated_data.calibration: n_c cases per cell x 5 S0 repeats, drawn like the Dev-B cases, independent of them; delta(N) and h(n_c) are computed from it with the existing functions
simulated_data.oracle: 50 cases per cell, S0 majority of 5 repeats against one candidate run, as in 009b; labels with the existing oracle and rq9 functions

tango_score.rule: Tango (1998) score interval for a paired difference of proportions; one-sided lower bound at level alpha

exact_conditional.rule: Condition on the observed number of discordant pairs d in the cell; one-sided exact binomial lower bound for q = p10 / (p10 + p01); the delta bound is (d / n_c) (2 q_lower - 1).
exact_conditional.caveat: Exact for q given d. For a margin on delta the discordance rate is a nuisance parameter, so the delta bound is approximate.

percentile_bootstrap.rule: cell paired bootstrap percentile, as in the current code
percentile_bootstrap.use: one demonstration condition only: baseline a, null_all_cells, n_c = 70, m_c = 0.05, main dependence; reported, not used for Go

baselines.a_s0_extreme: 009b S0 structure from the S0 calibration case rates (ceiling and floor cells kept as a stress test)
baselines.b_mid_range: S0-prime case rates from the Ticket 012 stage-0 records. Ten cases per cell, so the rates give a shape for the grid, not estimates; a Go under b needs an S0-prime baseline pilot before a confirmatory study.

effects.applies_to: Every candidate of a simulated pool gets the scenario's effect, except in the empirical scenario, where each candidate draws one.
effects.room_cells: cells whose baseline mean rate is at most 0.9

loss_cell_placements.realistic: the cell with the highest baseline mean rate (ties: the earlier cell in evidencegate.eval_data.CELLS)
loss_cell_placements.worst: the cell with the largest baseline variance p (1 - p), p = the cell's baseline mean rate (ties: the earlier cell in evidencegate.eval_data.CELLS)
loss_cell_placements.why_worst: a loss in a near-perfect cell is the easiest to detect because its baseline noise is small, so the realistic placement alone would understate the false-accept rate
loss_cell_placements.use: every scenario with a loss cell is run with both placements; null_all_cells has no loss cell and is run once

effects.no_global_one_cell_minus_m: the loss cell (each placement) delta_c = -m_c; an equal positive shift in the room cells other than the loss cell brings the target delta to 0
effects.global_up_one_cell_minus_m: the loss cell (each placement) delta_c = -m_c; an equal positive shift in the room cells other than the loss cell brings the target delta to +0.10
effects.global_up_one_cell_minus_2m: the loss cell (each placement) delta_c = -2 m_c; an equal positive shift in the room cells other than the loss cell brings the target delta to +0.10
effects.empirical: each candidate draws one v1 proposer candidate's cell effects with replacement

useful_representative.rule: delta_c = +0.10 in every cell whose baseline mean rate is at most 0.9, 0 elsewhere
useful_representative.role: the scenario for the joint-power criterion of Go

effects.realized_effects: After clipping, each candidate's true cell deltas are recomputed from its case rates; labels use the realized values. A scenario whose target delta cannot be reached because the room cells lack room is marked infeasible for that baseline and reported.
effects.inadmissible: a candidate whose realized true rates give delta <= 0 or some delta_c <= -m_c (the boundary belongs to the null)
effects.useful: a candidate whose realized true rates give delta > 0 and every delta_c > -m_c

dependence.note: Each assumption is varied on its own as a sensitivity; the main condition uses the first value of each.
shared_baseline: one S0 draw shared by all candidates in a simulated pool
seed_coupling_l1_l2: latent correlation 0.5 between the outcomes of the L1 and L2 case of one family and seed group
idea_groups: the 29-group size structure of the 009b pool: candidates in a group share one effect draw (empirical scenario only)

mc_se.formula: For a rate estimated over R pools as p = sum_r a_r / sum_r n_r (a_r events among n_r eligible candidates in pool r): SE = sqrt( R / (R - 1) * sum_r (a_r - p * n_r)^2 ) / sum_r n_r. Pools are the independent units; candidates within a pool share the S0 draw.
mc_se.binomial_check: When every pool has the same n_r, this is close to sqrt(p (1 - p) / (R n_r)) only under independence within pools; the pool formula is the one used.

gates.C4: as gates.gate_c4, with delta(N) from the simulated calibration (N = 6 n_c)
gates.C5: C4 and every cell delta_c >= -h(n_c), h from the simulated calibration (rq9.cell_threshold_h)
gates.C6_IUT: C4 and, in every cell, the one-sided lower bound of delta_c > -m_c; computed with each cell bound method, Go uses the primary

SAGE.original_rule: commit when Delta_lambda = w - lambda * l > 0, p_lambda = P[Bin(w + l, lambda / (1 + lambda)) >= w] < alpha, and rho = l / n_S <= tau; lambda, tau and alpha tuned on held-out data; applied repeatedly against the current incumbent
simplifications_here: one admission round against S0 only (no incumbent updates)
lambda, tau and alpha fixed before the simulation instead of tuned
w and l are counted over all Dev-B pairs (no cells); n_S = pairs where S0 succeeds
SAGE.tau_note: tau = 0.05 is our choice, fixed before the simulation; the SAGE paper tuned lambda, tau and alpha on held-out data.

SAGE_cell.rule: SAGE (same lambda, tau, alpha) and, in every cell, rho_c = l_c / n_S,c <= tau, with rho_c = 0 when n_S,c = 0
SAGE_cell.note: our construction; not in the SAGE paper

credit_type.original_rule: admit when the paired 95% lower bound of the error reduction (b - c) / n, with variance (b + c) / n^2 - (b - c)^2 / n^3, is > 0, and the share of cases in C (cases the incumbent answers correctly) that the candidate gets wrong is <= epsilon = 0.005
simplifications_here: one error kind: all Dev-B cases (the paper tests per error kind)
C = cases where S0 succeeds in the simulated Dev-B run

metrics: share of inadmissible candidates among the accepted
Useful acceptance rate (useful_representative: joint power; empirical: among useful candidates)
expected gain per proposal: mean over candidates of accept x realized delta
cost: Dev-B episodes = (candidates + 1) x cells x n_c
Oracle label uncertainty: share of candidates whose simulated oracle interval crosses a label boundary
coverage of each cell lower bound at the realized delta_c (exact_conditional and tango_score)

decision.unit: a combination (baseline, gate, n_c, m_c) under the main dependence condition; for C6_IUT the cell bound is the primary

false_accept_definition.infeasible: a (baseline, scenario, placement) whose target delta cannot be reached is reported as infeasible and left out of the maximum

decision.point_estimate: Go compares the Monte Carlo point estimates with the thresholds.

borderline.rule: A combination with any criterion point estimate within 2 MC SE of its threshold (|estimate - threshold| < 2 SE, SE by the monte_carlo.mc_se formula) is marked borderline. A borderline combination is reported but not counted toward Go.

decision.go: In baseline a or b, at least one combination that is not borderline meets all three thresholds at once.
decision.budget_note: With 40 candidates and S0, Dev-B = 41 x 6 x n_c: 17220 at n_c = 70, 36900 at 150, 73800 at 300, 147600 at 600. Only n_c <= 300 fits the budget; n_c = 600 is reported for the shape only.
decision.no_go: Record it as the result. Keep C5. Add no new statistical method.
decision.after_go: confirmatory study D (new pool, new incidents, pre-registered); under baseline b, an S0-prime baseline pilot comes before D
decision.no_changes_after_results: Margins, budget, thresholds and scenarios are not changed after any simulation result is seen.

limitations: ES is not simulated. 009b S0's ES sits at the floor or the ceiling, but S0-prime showed both an ES improvement and an ES regression as observable in all six cells, so an ES simulation is left as follow-up work.
Baseline b is a stylized mid-range structure resampled from ten S0-prime cases per cell. It is not an estimate of S0-prime and can understate the heterogeneity between cases.

The exact unconditional bound of Chan and Zhang (1999) is not included because of its computing cost over the grid; the exact conditional bound is approximate for a margin on delta and its coverage is reported instead.
Candidate run-to-run variation is not observed in any record; candidates are simulated with the same Bernoulli noise as S0.
SAGE and the credit-type gate are simplified to one round and fixed parameters; their papers' results are not reproduced here.
